openings.claim: Two removable, opposed strip-jaw clamps could carry sideways load through distributed pad friction while avoiding the observed concentrated left-corner preload.
openings.delta: Change the action from corner tightening to matched, small preload increments at opposed mid-edge contacts. Pair the four strips into upper/lower jaws, drill only strips, and use bolts outside the fixture edges. Pad fixture contacts; tie removable assemblies together with cord and park them clear of the opening. Nearest rival: concentrated corner pressure provides sufficient friction despite hatch rocking.
openings.prediction: If distributed preload matters, matched clamps will arrest sideways motion before opposite-corner lift reaches 2 mm, whereas concentrating equivalent tightening at the left contact will cause earlier lift. Tightening is only an approximate preload comparison; it cannot establish equal force.
openings.probe: First verify accessible rim undersides, bolt reach, strip overlap and pad placement without modifying hatch, rim or seal; otherwise park this design. Use one available trial for a reversible left-biased versus matched tightening observation, stopping at visible lift or seal distress. Then use eleven closure/pull trials: initial closure followed by ten opening cycles, with the last closure disturbed by the supplied right-contact card. Record marked displacement under 20 N, corner lift, reopening time and visible seal condition. All parts must be recoverable and entirely clear when open.
assumptions: Rim access, bolt lengths and strip stiffness permit stable jaws; these are unprovided indispensable geometry/capacity facts.
The initial comparison fits one closure/pull trial and leaves eleven for outcome testing.

Defeat conditions include slipping beyond 1 mm, reopening beyond 30 seconds, seal tearing, obstruction, or inability to fabricate within ninety minutes and observe within twenty. A successful probe would support only this fixture configuration.

assessment: A conditional mechanical candidate warrants a geometry check before fabrication. Pressure distribution could fail under the right-contact disturbance; no stipulated observation demonstrates clamp feasibility or outcome compliance. This is a probe, not deployment.
